paper_source.anchor: Section 5.1, Table 1; Appendix Tables 3, 6, 7, and 8 (S5.SS1, S5.T1, A1.T3, A1.T6-A1.T8)

exact_scope: Matched HSVL-versus-HIQL reproduction or falsification on HumanoidMaze-giant for C4 and on both AntMaze-giant and visual-AntMaze-giant for conjunctive C5, using preregistered seeds 0-3, matched datasets/configurations, 1,000,000 state updates or 500,000 visual updates, 50 evaluation episodes per task and seed, and uncertainty reconstructed from raw seed outputs.
decision_basis: Each accepted comparison requires both methods, four fixed seeds, paper-scale optimization, matched datasets and evaluation episodes, and seed-level uncertainty; paper numbers alone are not evidence.

The released state HSVL configuration specifies 1,000,000 JAX updates, while the official visual HIQL command specifies 500,000 convolutional updates and eval_on_cpu=0; these are accelerator-scale workloads.

The released HSVL agent constructs Identity state encoders and its disclosed HSVL configuration exposes no visual encoder field, whereas the pinned HIQL release explicitly uses impala_small for visual-AntMaze-giant.
C5 is conjunctive, so a state-only AntMaze result cannot substitute for the missing visual comparison.
blockers: Faithful four-seed giant-task training is GPU-bound, but every GPU flavor is forbidden by campaign policy.
The pinned public HSVL release does not expose the visual encoder integration needed to reproduce the paper's visual HSVL arm exactly.
A CPU-reduced model, fewer updates, fewer seeds, or one C5 task would remain toy or incomplete.
next_step: Stop C4 and C5 as BLOCKED. Do not launch local training, HF cpu-upgrade, or GPU work; retain this audit as source/protocol feasibility evidence only.
